newsitem.title: USA: India IOC in Iraq 3.6 mln bbls crude deal.
newsitem.headline: India IOC in Iraq 3.6 mln bbls crude deal.

text.p: The latest crude contract approved by U.N.-appointed overseers under the oil-for-food accord puts Iraq at the monetary cap of $1 billion for the first 90-day period of the six-month deal, U.N. sources said Thursday.
U.N. overseers okayed the 34th contract for Iraq to sell Indian Oil Corp, the state-owned oil company, 3.6 million barrels of crude, or 40,000 barrels per day over a 90-day period.
The U.N. official said part of the Indian Oil Corp sale would stretch into the second 90-day tranche of the oil accord.
U.N. sources said the Indian Oil Corp contract was one that had been under active consideration in recent days.

Overseers have been working to top out the first period of the accord at the $1 billion cap, a task made more difficult with the recent slide in world oil prices ahead of the first tranche's expiration on March 9.

"Iraq is allowed to sell a total of $1.07 billion or oil in the first period, included in that is a pipeline fee for Turkey. This last contract puts them at $1.06 billion, very close to the cap," said a U.N. official.
Sources said there would be no more contracts for the first period, and all futures contracts would apply to the second 90-days.

Terms of the oil accord have permitted Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil from December 10 for an initial six-month period. Proceeds from the accord will mostly be used for purchases of humanitarian aid for civilians suffering from six years of sanctions slapped on Baghdad after it invaded Kuwait.
